name: Greece

flag.description: Nine equal horizontal stripes alternating blue and white, with a blue square canton bearing a white cross in the upper hoist corner.
flag.symbolism: The nine stripes are traditionally said to match the syllables of 'Eleftheria i Thanatos' ('Freedom or Death'); the cross stands for Greek Orthodox Christianity.

hook: Nine blue and white stripes, one per syllable of 'Freedom or Death', with a cross in the corner: Uruguay has a sun in the corner instead.
trivia: The striped design dates from 1822, but until 1978 a plain white cross on blue served as the flag on land.
Greeks often call the flag the 'Galanolefki', meaning 'the blue and white'.
